To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a methodology for estimating local income distributions using tax micro-data that can be applied to any country with a tax system similar to the Spanish one and we have used this methodology to compute income inequality measures for Spanish municipalities.

the proposed methodology allows to derive a representative sample of income tax returns at the local level, and that the resulting estimates are consistent with official data and with other available estimates.

1) we provide the first local income distribution estimates for Spanish municipalities; 2) these local distributions can be used to compute local income inequality measures; 3) these measures show a high degree of spatial heterogeneity and a clear spatial correlation with local unemployment and poverty rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology that allows the estimation of local income distributions using tax microdata.
the estimation of local income distributions in Spanish municipalities.

the following issues: 1) the estimation of income distributions at the local level, 2) the use of tax data for the estimation of income distribution, and 3) the use of local income distributions for inequality analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results show a clear and significant heterogeneity in income distributions across municipalities and that the most unequal municipalities are located in the south of Spain.
, although the Spanish regions are very different, they all share a similar income distribution.
our results show that, in general, the income inequality in Spanish municipalities is lower than that of the whole country, and the income distribution is more concentrated in the central regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methodology developed in this paper provides the basis to derive a set of local income distributions for a large number of Spanish municipalities.
the methodology presented in this paper provides an estimation of the personal income distribution at the local level, which is a useful tool for income inequality analysis.

the methodology developed here is a useful and practical tool that allows us to estimate the distribution of local personal incomes and that it can be applied to other European countries where income taxes are progressive and the data is available.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of micro-data allows us to obtain more accurate estimates of local income distributions than the use of official data, and that the differences between both approaches are more relevant for small localities than for large municipalities.
the methodology is feasible and that it provides valuable information on the income distribution at the local level.

the use of tax microdata allows us to obtain a representative sample of income distribution at a local level and to compute a wide range of indicators that are very useful to analyze local welfare and wellbeing, as well as to study the spatial distribution of income.
